title: Procurement catalyst matrix and LLM adoption signal playbook
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Goal: produce an actionable playbook and a procurement catalyst matrix that help Sales, Solutions, and Procurement teams detect when customers are primed to switch models/providers and identify the signals that precede enterprise adoption of emerging open LLM variants.

Scope:
- Synthesize buyer interviews, telemetry, and competitor feature/time-to-market to identify 12 high-confidence signals that reliably precede procurement conversations (e.g., latency tolerance windows, cost-per-1M-token inflection, quantization acceptance, data residency triggers).
- Produce a ranked Procurement Catalyst Matrix linking signals -> likely buyer cohorts -> economic thresholds -> recommended platform responses (rate-limit adjustments, dedicated outreach, canary offers).
- Deliverables: one-page playbook for GTM, a slide deck with evidence and recommended experiments, and a lightweight dashboard spec for automated signal alerting in Console.

Approach / Methodology:
1) Field research: schedule 10–15 qualitative interviews with mid-market and enterprise product leads (targeted cohorts: fintech, healthtech, platform teams). Capture procurement decision drivers, SLA tolerances, and fallback acceptance criteria.
2) Telemetry analysis: partner with Eng (ENG-2244) to query signup/usage funnels for customers that migrated models in past 12 months; infer signal patterns (API latency distributions, burst usage, embedding request ratios).
3) Competitive scan: map 20 open and closed-source model launches to feature release cadence and price inflection points; annotate where vendors introduced fallbacks or specialized quantization/cost tiers.
4) Hypothesis testing: design 3 small experiments (targeted trials, feature gating, pricing probes) to validate top 3 signals in a 6-week pilot.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Prioritize signals that are observable in telemetry to enable automation; accept that some high-fidelity signals (procurement committee composition) will remain human-sourced and require SDR/SE inputs.
- Balance precision vs recall: early-warning signals should err on recall (more noise) but be paired with a human validation step to avoid churn.
- Cost of false positives: outreach and incentives to customers who were not ready—minimize by thresholding and staging contact (email -> SE outreach -> tailored offer).

Success metrics:
- Pilot sensitivity: detect >= 70% of customers who enter procurement cycle within 90 days.
- Precision: at least 40% of alerted customers convert to meaningful sales conversation within 30 days.
- Operational: dashboard alert noise rate < 1 per 100 active accounts per month.

Risks and mitigations:
- Telemetry gaps (blocked by ENG backlog): mitigate with manual instrumented exports and 3 customer interviews as fallback evidence.
- Vendor sensitivity/legal: anonymize competitor references in GTM collateral.
- Signal drift: schedule quarterly recalibration and tie to Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1 (current): finalize interview guide, secure access to telemetry exports (ENG-2244), competitive data sources.
- Week 2–3: run interviews (Maia lead), compile thematic codes, produce initial list of 20 candidate signals.
- Week 4: implement telemetry queries, validate top 10 signals, draft Procurement Catalyst Matrix.
- Week 5: pilot cohort selection, design 3 experiments with Sales/SE, build dashboard spec.
- Week 6: pilot run and initial evaluation; deliver final playbook + deck for leadership review.
